pages.title: Help - Broadcast control
pages.description: Broadcast control is where you go on air from your phone: send your microphone, your camera, a ready audio or video file or the whole screen to other people, then hand them the link, the QR code or a file so that they can watch and listen. The same screen shows how many are connected and ends the broadcast.
pages.body: Help index / Broadcast control Broadcast control What this is for Broadcast control is where you go on air from your phone: send your microphone, your camera, a ready audio or video file or the whole screen to other people, then hand them the link, the QR code or a file so that they can watch and listen. The same screen shows how many are connected and ends the broadcast. In this order Open Live Broadcast from the programs menu, the programs panel, a Quick Settings tile or a home-screen widget. If it is not offered there, switch it on first in Settings, on the Media tab, in the Broadcast group. The screen 1 opens with Audio only chosen and stays awake while it is open. Choose what to send: sound only 3 , the camera with sound 4 or the camera alone 5 . A camera mode shows the camera picture 2 and, when the phone has several cameras, the list of cameras 6 to pick from. Adjust the title, the port and the sound quality in the settings card 7 if you need to, then press Start broadcast 8 . The first start asks for the microphone, the camera and notifications - allow what the message names. To send something other than the camera and the microphone, press Broadcast a file 9 and pick an audio or video file, or Broadcast the screen 10 and confirm the system question about showing the screen. While you are on air, the number of listeners 12 is shown at the top. Switch the camera 14 and the microphone 15 off and on, change the camera 16 , let the screen go to sleep 17 or light the scene (18, 19). Press Stop broadcast 22 when you are done. Give the viewers the broadcast: show the QR code 23 , copy the link 27 , send it on 29 or save it as a file 28 . A protected broadcast also shows a password 25 , which you tell separately. Cast to my devices 21 and Send to watch 20 hand the live broadcast to your own other devices, and Guests 30 gives it to another account. The guide buttons (11, 31, 32) open pages on the site. The elements Before the broadcast 1 Broadcast Control The name of the screen, which has two states: before the broadcast and on air. Before the broadcast the screen shows what to send and the settings. On air it shows the live controls and the ways to share. A block that does not apply at the moment is hidden, not greyed out. The screen is kept awake while it is open, until you let it go to sleep (17). 2 Camera picture What your camera sees and, on air, what is being sent. Before the start it lets you choose a camera by what it shows. It appears when a camera mode is chosen and the camera is allowed; if you refuse the camera, the area stays empty and the screen asks only once per visit. On air it shows the picture that goes out. It is hidden for sound only and for a file or screen broadcast, which do not use the camera. 3 Audio only Sends only the sound of the microphone. The default mode. It needs the microphone only. You can pick another mode on air too: the broadcast is then reopened in that mode, and viewers reopen the stream by the updated link or QR code. 4 Camera + audio Sends the picture of the camera together with the sound. Needs the camera and the microphone. On air the camera and the microphone can be switched off one by one (14, 15). 5 Camera only Sends the picture of the camera without sound. Needs the camera. In some editions Android also asks for the microphone, although no sound is sent. 6 Camera Chooses which camera of the phone sends the picture. One button per camera the phone offers: back, front or external. They appear with a camera mode, once the phone has listed its cameras. On air a tap changes the camera at once. The choice is remembered for the next time. 7 Broadcast settings The options of the broadcast, kept next to the Start button. The card holds the same options as the Broadcast group of the Media settings: whether live broadcasting is on, the title of your broadcast, the bit rate, the port, the audio format, the microphone gain, the feedback guard and whether this screen opens by itself when a broadcast starts. Changes are saved at once, and a title or port you have just typed is used by the broadcast you start next. The card is hidden on air, because the settings of a running broadcast cannot change. 8 Start broadcast Goes on air in the chosen mode. If the broadcast needs an access the phone has not given yet - the microphone, the camera or notifications - the system asks first, and a message names what is missing if you refuse. If the broadcast cannot start, for example because the phone cannot open the port, a message says why and the screen stays as it was. Once you are on air, the button gives way to the live controls and the sharing block. 9 Broadcast a file Broadcasts a ready audio or video file instead of the microphone and the camera. Opens the system file picker for audio and video files. The picked file is played out as a live broadcast, without the microphone or the camera, so the controls for them are not shown. A file that does not open or has nothing to play is refused with a message. The button is shown only before you start, and only in editions that can broadcast. 10 Broadcast the screen Broadcasts what is shown on the screen of the phone. The system asks for confirmation every time. The permission is for one broadcast only and is never kept. If you decline, nothing starts. During a screen broadcast the buttons for the camera, the microphone and the screen are not shown, because blanking the app would blank what the viewers see. 11 How to go on air Opens the guide to going on air on the site. Shown before the broadcast starts. The page opens in your browser, so it needs the internet; nothing changes in the app. While you are on air 12 Listener count How many devices are connected to your broadcast right now. The number appears only while you are on air and follows people connecting and leaving. 13 Feedback warning Tells you why the sound got quieter: a listener's speaker is feeding back into your microphone. It shows in red only when the Feedback guard has turned the microphone down. That happens when someone plays your broadcast aloud next to the microphone and the sound would build up into a squeal. Move that device away or lower its volume, and the warning goes. The guard is an option of the Broadcast settings. 14 Camera on and off Turns the picture off and on without ending the broadcast. Shown for broadcasts with the camera. The button says whether the camera is on or off at the moment. With the camera off, viewers see a black picture and the sound goes on. 15 Microphone on and off Mutes and unmutes the sound. Shown only for Camera + audio. The button says whether the microphone is on or off at the moment. With it off, viewers see the picture without sound. 16 Switch Camera Changes which camera sends the picture. Opens a list of every camera the phone offers, not only the front and the back one; tap a camera to switch at once. The choice is remembered for the next broadcast. 17 Screen off Lets the screen go to sleep while the broadcast goes on. Where the camera can keep working in the background, and for sound only, the button stops keeping the screen awake, so the display sleeps after the usual time. In editions where the camera works only while the app is visible, the button is called Blank screen: it covers the app with a black screen and a dim clock while the display stays on. Tap the black screen or press Back to return. It is not shown for file and screen broadcasts. 18 Flashlight Lights the scene with the flash of the camera. Shown only when the camera on air has a flash and is switched on; a front camera usually has none. The button says whether the flashlight is on or off. 19 Bright frame Lights your face with a bright white frame around the screen. A white border over the edges of the screen, with the brightness of this window raised - useful when you film yourself in the dark. The preview, the buttons and the QR code stay usable under it. Only the brightness of this window rises, never the brightness setting of the phone. The frame goes out when the broadcast ends or the camera stops. Shown for broadcasts with the camera of the phone. 20 Send to watch Plays this live broadcast on the paired watch. Shown on air, when the watch companion is switched on and the phone supports it. It sends the broadcast to the watch and opens it there. A message tells you when the watch is not reachable or does not answer. 21 Cast to my devices Asks your other devices to play this broadcast. Shown on air, while the broadcast travels through your exchange server (see My devices). The button opens the list Play on with your devices that can play it, each marked online or offline; tick one or more and press Cast to my devices. Each device receives a request it can accept or decline, and a message tells you which one is playing or why it refused. 22 Stop Broadcast Ends the broadcast. The listeners are disconnected, the camera and the microphone are released, and the screen returns to the state before the start, with the settings card back. The notification of the broadcast has its own Stop button. Sharing the broadcast 23 Broadcast Descriptor QR Code A QR code that hands the broadcast to a device nearby. The other device scans it to add the broadcast: in Streams, open the menu and choose Import stream (QR / file). Tap the code to show it across the full screen, so that it can be scanned from across the room; tap again or press Back to return. When the mode changes on air, the code is replaced, also when it is open. The code never carries the password. 24 Broadcast link The address your broadcast is served at. The text can be selected. The address works for devices that can reach your phone over the network. Copy link (27) copies it, and Send (29) passes on a link that opens the broadcast in the app, built from the same data as the QR code. 25 Link password The password of a protected broadcast, told apart from the link. Shown only for a protected broadcast. Neither the link, the file nor the QR code carries it, so you give it to the person separately, by voice or in another message. 26 New password Makes a new password; the old one stops working. Use it when the password has reached someone who should not have it. A message reminds you to tell the new password separately from the link. 27 Copy Link Copies the link of the broadcast. A message confirms the copy. A protected broadcast is copied as the full link instead of the bare address, so that the other device knows a password is needed and asks for it. 28 Export File Saves the broadcast as a small file you can pass on. The system asks where to save it. Someone who receives the file adds the broadcast with Import stream (QR / file) in Streams. A message tells you whether the file was saved. 29 Send to Sends the link through any app you choose. Opens the system list of apps and contacts. The link opens the broadcast in FastMediaSorter on the other device; where the app is not installed, it opens a page on the site instead. 30 Guests Gives the live broadcast to another account of your exchange server. Shown only for a protected broadcast announced through the exchange server by a member account. The dialog Give the broadcast to a guest takes the guest's login (3 to 64 letters, digits, dots, dashes or underscores) with Give, and lists everyone who has it with the answer of the server - waiting, given or refused. Withdraw takes the broadcast from one guest alone. 31 How to watch this Opens the page you can forward to whoever receives the broadcast. The page explains how to watch with the link, the QR code or the file. It opens in the browser and needs the internet. 32 How broadcasting works between devices Opens the page about how broadcasting works between devices. A page on the site, opened in the browser. It needs the internet and changes nothing in the app. Related Main screen Screen Streams Screen My devices Screen Settings: Media Screen Player Screen Wear Companion Screen Chromecast Casting and Live Broadcast Guide Streams on a TV, a Watch or a VR Headset, and Tuning In to a Live Broadcast Guide Listening Through the Watch and Broadcasting from It Guide Help index Fast Media Sorter, 2026-10-18 Help index Ask a question or report a problem

pages.title: Help - Saved authorizations
pages.description: Saved authorizations lists the sign-ins that the in-app web browser keeps for websites, so the app can fetch content from sites that need an account without asking you to sign in again. Here you add, rename, renew and delete them. Open it from Settings, General tab, Authorization and accounts.
pages.body: Help index / Saved authorizations Saved authorizations What this is for Saved authorizations lists the sign-ins that the in-app web browser keeps for websites, so the app can fetch content from sites that need an account without asking you to sign in again. Here you add, rename, renew and delete them. Open it from Settings, General tab, Authorization and accounts. In this order Press + Add authorization 2 and choose a site from the list, or Enter address manually for another one. Sign in on the page that opens 12 the way you would in a browser, then press Save authorization 13 . Give the account a name you will recognize 15 and press Save. The account appears under its site in the list 5 . To add a second account for the same site, press the plus in the site's header 7 . When a site stops accepting a saved sign-in, press Sign in again 9 . Rename account 10 changes only the name shown here. Delete saved authorization 11 removes a sign-in you no longer need, after you confirm. Nothing on this screen needs saving: every change applies at once, and Back 1 simply leaves. The elements The list 1 Back Leaves the list. Everything on this screen is applied the moment you do it, so there is nothing to confirm when you leave. 2 + Add authorization Starts a new sign-in for a website. The first choice is a list of known sites; the last line, Enter address manually, asks for a full web address that starts with http or https. After you pick a site, its sign-in page opens in the sign-in window described at the end of this page. Addresses on Google domains open in a Custom Tabs browser instead; if no such browser is installed, a Browser needed window explains what to install. 3 Help Opens the help for this screen. It sits in the overflow menu of the toolbar, because it is rarely needed. Shortcut F1 4 Explanation A short reminder of what a saved authorization is. Each entry stores the cookies of one account on one site. An entry marked Not authorized (you declined) was created when you chose Do not ask in a sign-in prompt, and it stops the prompt from appearing for that site again. To add a second account for the same site, use + Add authorization or the plus in the site's header. 5 Sign-in list All saved sign-ins, grouped by site. Every site has a header with its name; Instagram, Threads and Facebook are recognized by name, other sites show their address. The accounts of that site follow the header. The list stays empty until you save your first sign-in. 6 No saved authorizations Tells you that nothing is saved yet. The note replaces the list while there are no entries. Press + Add authorization in the toolbar to save the first one. Sites and accounts 7 Add another account Adds another account for the same site. The plus in a site's header opens that site's sign-in page. Use it when you have two accounts on one site and want both to be available. 8 Account entry One saved sign-in: its name and its details. Under the name, a grey line shows how many cookies are stored, when the entry was saved and when it was last used, or not yet used. An entry called Not authorized (you declined) is not a real sign-in: it only remembers that you declined to sign in to that site, so the app stops offering. It has the delete button only; delete it to be asked again. 9 Sign in again Signs in to the same site again and renews the entry. Use it when a site no longer accepts the saved sign-in, for example because it expired or you changed the password. The sign-in page opens with no old cookies, so the site starts from a clean state. The button is not shown for declined entries. 10 Rename account Changes the name the account has in this list. A small window with the current name opens. Type a new one and press OK; an empty name is ignored. The sign-in itself is not touched. The button is not shown for declined entries. 11 Delete saved authorization Removes a saved sign-in from the app. A window asks Delete sign-in for and the account name, with OK and Cancel. After OK, the cookies stored for that account are gone and the entry disappears from the list. Undo The saved sign-in is lost and cannot be restored; your account on the site is not touched. To get it back, sign in again with + Add authorization or the plus in the site's header. Sign-in window 12 Sign-in page The site's own sign-in page, shown inside the app. Sign in the way the site asks, including any code it sends you. The page starts signed out: old cookies are cleared first, so a leftover session cannot get in the way. Depending on the Secure sensitive screens setting, the window is hidden from screenshots and the recent apps view. 13 Save authorization Stores the sign-in you just made. The button stays dimmed until the page has set at least one cookie, so sign in first; if you press it too early, the app reminds you to sign in. After the press, a window asks you to name the account. 14 Cancel Closes the sign-in window and saves nothing. Use it if you opened the wrong site or changed your mind. 15 Name this account Gives the saved sign-in a name you will recognize. The field already holds a name that the app could read from the sign-in, or Default account if it could not read any. Press Save to store the entry; if the same account of that site is already stored, the app updates that entry instead of adding a second one. The sign-in window is then cleared of cookies and cache, and the entry appears in the list. pages.title: Help - Add Resource
pages.description: Add Resource is where you connect a new place with your files to the app: a folder on the device, a network share, an SFTP or FTP server, a cloud folder, an internet stream or your watch. Pick a type, fill in a short form, and the new resource appears in the list on the main screen.
headings: Cloud folder pickers (Google Drive, OneDrive, Dropbox)
pages.body: Help index / Add Resource Add Resource What this is for Add Resource is where you connect a new place with your files to the app: a folder on the device, a network share, an SFTP or FTP server, a cloud folder, an internet stream or your watch. Pick a type, fill in a short form, and the new resource appears in the list on the main screen. In this order Choose what to add: Local Folder 2 for this device, Network Folder 3 for an SMB share, SFTP / FTP 4 , Cloud Storage 5 , Stream 6 , Paired watch 7 or From my devices 8 . Types that are switched off in Settings or missing from your edition are not listed, and if you press Add on the main screen while a type tab is open, that type's form opens at once. Device folder: press SCAN 12 to get suggestions or Add Manually 13 to pick a folder yourself, tick what you want in the list 14 , then press Add to Resources 11 . Network share: enter the server address 17 , or find it with Scan Network 16 . Add the username 18 and password 19 , check them with Test connection 20 , choose the share with Scan host 21 or type its name 22 , then press Add This Resource 27 . SFTP or FTP: choose the protocol 29 , enter the host 30 and the sign-in 31 , try Test Connection 32 , set the remote path 34 and press Add Resource 36 . Cloud storage: tap a provider 15 , sign in, then open folders with Enter 45 and press Select 46 on the one you want to add. Have a ready configuration from the Windows companion? Import from file 9 or Import by barcode 10 saves you typing all of this. Back 1 leaves the screen without adding anything that is not saved yet. The elements Choosing what to add 1 Back Leaves this screen without adding what you have not saved yet. From the type list or from any form, the button takes you back to the screen you came from, usually the main screen. It does not step back from a form to the type list - to choose another type, open Add again. What you typed in a form and did not add is dropped. Shortcut Esc / F10 2 Local Folder Adds a folder, or a collection of media, from this device. Opens the Local Folder form: let the app scan for folders that hold media, or pick any folder yourself, a memory card or USB drive included. This card is always here. When every remote source is switched off or missing from your edition, it is the only choice, so the screen skips the type list and opens this form straight away. 3 Network Folder Adds a shared folder from a PC or NAS over SMB. Opens the SMB form, which takes the server address, the sign-in and the share name. The card shows up only when SMB is available in your edition and switched on in Settings, General tab, Remote resources (SMB/(S)FTP/Cloud). 4 SFTP / FTP Adds a folder on an SFTP or FTP server. Opens the SFTP / FTP form, where you choose the protocol and sign in with a password or an SSH key. The card shows up when SFTP or FTP is available in your edition and switched on in Settings, General tab, Remote resources. The two import buttons are repeated at the top of that form. 5 Cloud Storage Adds a folder from Google Drive, OneDrive or Dropbox. Opens the list of cloud providers. Cloud storage is not part of every edition, and the card shows up only while at least one cloud provider is switched on in Settings, General tab, Remote resources. 6 Stream Adds an internet stream by its web address. Instead of a form on this screen, it opens the resource editor for a new stream. There you give the stream a name and its address (http, https or rtsp), and add a comment or a PIN if you want. It then joins your resources like any other. 7 Paired watch Adds your paired watch as a resource. A watch has no address or password, so the app asks for one thing only: a name (the suggestion is Watch). There is just one paired watch; if it is already in your resources you get a note instead of a duplicate. The card shows up only in editions that can work with a watch. 8 From my devices Attaches resources that your other devices publish. Opens a list of the resources your other devices share through your exchange server or Google Drive. Tick the ones you need and press Attach, or press Attach all listed to take everything on the list. The card is shown together with the SFTP / FTP card, because attached resources connect as SFTP resources. 9 Import from file Creates resources from a configuration file prepared on a PC. Pick the configuration file that the Windows companion saved. The app reads it, adds new resources, updates the ones that already exist, tells you how many changed and closes this screen. If the file carries no password, a window shows the server and asks for it first. A damaged file, or one made by a newer version, is refused with a message. 10 Import by barcode Creates resources from a QR code shown by the PC companion. Opens the camera to scan the code, then imports exactly as a file would. A pairing code from another phone's built-in SFTP server works here too - it fills in the SFTP / FTP form for you to check and save. The button is hidden on devices without a camera, VR headsets included; use the Import from file button there. 11 Add to Resources Saves the folders you ticked in the local list. The button appears only once the Local Folder form has something in its list. It adds every ticked row as a resource, tells you how many were added and closes the screen. With nothing ticked you get a reminder to select at least one. If your Quick Sort list is full, the resources are still added, but the surplus ones are left out of Quick Sort and the message says how many. Local folder and cloud storage 12 SCAN Looks for folders with media on this device. Builds a list of suggestions: the standard folders, folders that contain media, and collections such as Recent Media or All Music. Folders and collections you have already added are left out. Nothing is saved yet - tick what you want in the list below and press Add to Resources. 13 Add Manually Picks a folder or a collection yourself. Opens the Select Folder window. Its Virtual resources buttons (Recent Media, All Music, All Videos, Camera Photos, All Images, All Documents) add that collection at once and close this screen. Quick Select Common Folders offers the device root, DCIM, Pictures, Download, Documents and the WhatsApp, Telegram and Instagram folders; Removable media lists connected cards and drives; a path field (only where the app may read paths) and the system picker cover the rest. A folder you pick lands in the list below already ticked. When Android first needs All files access, a window explains it and lets you grant it or continue with limited access. 14 Resources to add: The folders found or picked, ready to be ticked and added. Each row has a checkbox, a name you can edit, the path, the file count and one letter per media type - tap a letter to switch that type on or off. Under them sit Mark for Quick Sort, Read-only mode, Scan subdirectories and All Files. A folder that cannot be written to cannot be marked for Quick Sort. The list stays hidden until the first folder arrives. 15 Select Cloud Provider Signs in to Google Drive, OneDrive or Dropbox, then lets you pick a folder. Every card shows Not connected, or Connected as and the account. Tap a provider: if you have signed in before, you choose an account or Add New Account, otherwise sign-in starts at once. When it succeeds, the folder picker opens (see the last group of this page). Network share (SMB) form 16 Scan Network Finds computers with shared folders on your local network. Opens the Network Discovery window and scans your local network. Pick a computer from its list: its address goes into Server IP and the app lists its shares for you. On some Android versions the app first asks for permission to reach devices on the local network. 17 Server IP The address of the computer or NAS that shares the folder. Type an IP address. The field starts with the first three numbers of your phone's own address, so usually you only add the last one. An empty or invalid address stops Test connection and Scan host with a message. 18 Username The account that is allowed to open the share. Type the name of the account on the server. A Windows domain, if you use one, goes under Additional Options. 19 Password The password of that account. It is saved with the resource, so the app can connect on its own later. While this form is open, the screen can be hidden from screenshots and the recent apps view, depending on the Secure sensitive screens setting. 20 Test connection Checks the address and the sign-in before you save. Connects with what you typed and shows Connection Test - Success or Connection Test - Failed in a window. Nothing is saved. 21 Scan host Lists the shared folders a server offers. Asks the server which shares it has and shows them in a list. Pick one and its name goes into the ShareName/subfolder field. The list also holds names you typed by hand earlier, marked with a tick, and a line to type a name yourself. If the server shows nothing, a message says so and you type the name instead. Fill in Server IP first, or you get a reminder. 22 ShareName/subfolder The shared folder to open, and optionally a subfolder inside it. For example Common or Photos. Take it from the Scan host list or type it yourself; backslashes are turned into slashes. 23 Resource Name How the resource is called in your list. If you leave it empty, the app uses the share name. You can rename the resource later in its editor. 24 Content Scanning Conditions Decides which files of the share the app looks at. A collapsible section with five choices. Scan subdirectories looks for media in all nested folders. All Files shows every file type, not only media. Show subfolders separately lists subfolders as items you tap to enter. Disable thumbnails shows extension icons instead of previews. Remember file list for this resource keeps a copy of the list on the device for faster loading. 25 Media Types Chooses which kinds of files the resource shows. Tick Images, Videos, Audio, GIFs, Text, PDF, EPUB and DOC - only the types that are turned on in Settings and available in your edition are listed. The button at the top, Custom at first, opens Resource Profile with ready sets: Audio Library, Video Library, Photo Storage, Documents and File Manager Mode. All Files in the section above ticks every type and locks the boxes. 26 Additional Options Optional extras: Quick Sort, read-only, a comment, a PIN, the domain and the port. Mark for Quick Sort registers the share as a destination for sorting. Read-only mode blocks copy, move and delete on it, and switches Quick Sort off. Comment is a note for yourself, and PIN Code (Optional) protects the resource with 4-6 digits. Domain is for Windows domain accounts, and Port is 445 unless your server listens elsewhere. 27 Add This Resource Saves the share as a resource. Saves the sign-in details, adds the resource, shows a message and closes this screen. If the share cannot be reached right away, you are told so, but the resource is still added - check the share name and access, then fix them in the editor. SFTP / FTP form 28 How to publish PC folders to Android Opens the guide for publishing PC folders to the app. The link sits at the top of the form next to the two import buttons and opens the companion's setup guide in your browser. Use it when you have not published any PC folders yet and have nothing to import. 29 Select Protocol: Chooses SFTP (secure, over SSH) or plain FTP. SFTP uses port 22 and FTP uses port 21; the port field follows your choice unless you typed another number. FTP is not encrypted, so prefer SFTP when the server offers it. The Server verification block below applies to SFTP only and is hidden for FTP. 30 Host The name or IP address of the server, and its port. Type the host name or the address. The port is filled in for you (22 for SFTP, 21 for FTP); change it only if your server listens elsewhere. An empty or invalid host is refused with a message. 31 Sign-in method Signs in with a password or with an SSH key. Password asks for the username and the password. SSH Key asks for the username and the private key - paste the key text or press Load File to read it from a file - plus a passphrase if the key has one. SSH keys work with SFTP only; FTP always uses a password. 32 Test Connection Checks the address and the sign-in before you save. Connects with what you typed and reports success or failure in a window. When the server shows its host key and the verification field is still empty, the window offers Pin Host Key, which copies the key into Server verification for you. 33 Server verification (optional) Locks the connection to one genuine server. Paste the server's host key fingerprint in SHA256 format and the app refuses any other machine that answers at this address. That protects you from someone pretending to be your server. It is optional and applies to SFTP only; the easiest way to fill it is Test Connection and then Pin Host Key. 34 Remote Path The folder on the server that becomes the resource. For example /home/user/media, or / for everything the account can see. Right below it, Resource Name is the label in your list; if you leave it empty, the app makes one up. 35 Scanning, media types and additional options Three collapsible sections that work exactly as in the network share form. Content Scanning Conditions, Media Types and Additional Options hold the same choices as for an SMB share: subdirectories, All Files, thumbnails, media types with the profile button, Quick Sort, Read-only mode, a comment and a PIN. Open them only if the defaults do not suit you. 36 Add Resource Saves the server folder as a resource. Needs a host and at least one media type; otherwise a message tells you what is missing. After saving, the screen closes. If the server cannot be reached right away, the resource is still added and a message says it is unavailable for now, so you can correct the details later in the editor. Network Discovery dialog 37 Scan status Shows how far the search has come. While it works, the line shows the part of the network being checked and a counter. When the search ends it says Scan complete. 38 Found devices Lists devices on your network that offer file sharing. Each row shows the device name, its address and the services it offers - SMB, FTP or SFTP. Tap a row to use that device: its address goes into the Server IP field, the window closes and the app lists its shares. If nothing turns up, a note says No devices found yet; make sure you are on the same Wi-Fi and press Scan Again. 39 Stop Stops the search, or starts it again. While the scan runs, the button reads Stop and ends the search without closing the window. Once the scan has finished or been stopped, it reads Scan Again and searches once more. 40 Cancel Closes the window without choosing a device. A scan that is still running is stopped as well. Cloud folder pickers (Google Drive, OneDrive, Dropbox) 41 Pull down to refresh Reloads the folders of the level you are on. Drag the list down to load it again, for example after you created a folder in the cloud. The keyboard does the same. Shortcut Ctrl + Shift + R / Ctrl + F5 42 Add as destination Also marks the chosen folder for Quick Sort. When ticked, the folder you select becomes a Quick Sort destination as well as a resource. Tick it before you press Select; it starts unticked. 43 Scan subdirectories Includes everything inside the chosen folder. When ticked, which it is at the start, media is searched in all folders nested under the one you select. Untick it to look at the top level only. 44 Folder list The folders of your cloud storage, one level at a time. The toolbar shows the path you are in. Tap a row to go into that folder; each row also has its own Enter and Select buttons, and Back below the top level. If a level has no folders, a note says so. Shortcut Enter 45 Enter Opens the folder to show the folders inside it. Does the same as tapping the row. Use it to go down to the folder you really want before you press Select. 46 Select Adds this folder to your resources. Creates a cloud resource from the folder, using your Add as destination and Scan subdirectories choices and the media types enabled in Settings. You see Resource added and land on the main screen. A folder you added before is refused with a note. Undo Nothing in the cloud changes. To undo it, delete the resource on the main screen; the folder stays where it is. 47 Back Goes up one level. The button appears on rows below the top level. The toolbar arrow and the Back button of the device do the same, and from the top level they close the picker. Esc closes it too. Shortcut Backspace Related Main screen Screen Settings: General Screen Edit Resource Screen Saved authorizations Screen My devices Screen Streams Screen Adding Folders from Your Phone, Memory Card and USB Drive Guide Adding Network Folders and Cloud Storage as Sources Guide Sharing PC Folders with Fast Media Sorter & Sharing for Windows Guide Help index Fast Media Sorter, 2026-10-18 Help index Ask a question or report a problem

pages.title: First Launch and Setup Wizard
pages.description: How the welcome wizard walks you through language, theme, device profile, network and cloud sources, permissions and your default player the first time you open FastMediaSorter - and how to skip most of it with one tap.
headings: Page 1: meet the app, in your language and your look
Page 2: tell it what kind of device this is
Page 3: turn on the network and cloud folders you use
Page 4: choose what the app can do
Page 5: grant the permissions it asks for
Page 6: make it your default player (first run only)
Or skip ahead - the Enable all shortcut
Finish, and what happens right after
pages.body: Getting Started All editions Recipe #01 All editions - which pages appear depends on the edition First Launch and Setup Wizard The welcome wizard runs once, the first time you open FastMediaSorter, and walks you through language, theme, device profile , network and cloud sources, capabilities, permissions and your default player - or you can skip straight to the end with the Enable all button on its first page. Every choice it makes lives in Settings afterward, so nothing here is a one-way door. Why You'll Love This Everyone meets FastMediaSorter for the first time exactly once, and that first minute quietly decides a few things: which language you read it in, whether it can see your network drives, and whether Android starts opening your photos and videos in it from now on. The welcome wizard exists so you make those calls on purpose, in a couple of minutes, instead of finding them out by accident later. Nothing on these pages is final. Every choice you make here can be changed afterward in Settings , so there is no wrong tap - and if you would rather not answer a wizard's worth of questions at all, one button near the top does almost all of it for you. Before You Begin: Ingredients & Prerequisites FastMediaSorter freshly installed, in any edition - which wizard pages you see depends on which one you have. A few minutes, and if you plan to add network or cloud folders, their addresses or sign-in details close at hand. An internet connection if you turn on OCR or translation on the functionality page - both download a small engine the moment you switch them on. 1 Page 1: meet the app, in your language and your look The wizard opens the moment you launch FastMediaSorter for the first time and stays open until you finish it or tap Enable all . A row of dots above the bottom buttons shows how many pages there are and where you are; Previous and Next move between them, and Finish takes the place of Next on the last page. Every page answers to a fingertip just as well as to a keyboard, a D-pad or a mouse wheel, so a TV box or a car head unit with no touchscreen sets up the app exactly the same way a phone does. The first page introduces FastMediaSorter as a short list of roles rather than a list of features: File Manager ("Browse, copy, move and delete files"), a player card titled Media Player or, on an edition without video and audio, Photo Viewer , Any Source , One-Tap Sorting , and a catch-all More card. A build that ships the home-screen launcher leads with a Home screen card instead, and one that ships internet Streams or the watch app gets its own card for each of those too, rather than folding them into More . Every card's second line names only the media types, protocols and services your particular edition can actually open, so nothing pitched here is missing once you look for it. Two more controls share this page: a language button that names your current language and opens a searchable list when tapped, and an Auto / Light / Dark theme picker. Both take effect immediately, so you see the result before you decide anything else. The first wizard page: your role pitch, language and theme. Said no to the home screen? If a build offers to make FastMediaSorter your home screen and you decline, it remembers that - it will not ask again, not here and not the next few times you open Settings. 2 Page 2: tell it what kind of device this is FastMediaSorter asks "How will you use this device?" and lays out a row of profile tiles: Personal smartphone , Tablet & desktop mode , TV / media box , Car head unit , Audio player , Video player , E-book reader , Media player , Photo frame , VR headset , and Other / Custom . It has already picked one for you, marked (Recommended) , based on the hardware it detected - tap a different tile if it guessed wrong. Whichever tile is selected shows its whole description; every other tile stays clamped to one line, so the page does not turn into a wall of text. Tap the selected tile a second time to confirm it and move straight to the next page - a repeat tap means "this one, go on," the same as tapping Next would. Moving past this page applies that device profile 's whole settings preset, which decides what the pages that follow default to; anything you change afterward on your own still sticks. Picking TV / media box , Car head unit or Photo frame also leaves automatic power saving off, since those devices run on fixed power and a battery threshold would never trigger anyway - and Photo frame additionally turns off left-swipe-to-delete on a file row, to match the fact that this profile does not offer deletion at all. Choosing a device profile: the selected tile reads in full. 3 Page 3: turn on the network and cloud folders you use On the Standard, Legacy, VR and noLegal editions, a Network resources page follows: "Add media from network shares and remote storage." Three group switches sit underneath, each one turning a whole family of sources on or off at once, with a plain-language example beside it: Local network (Ethernet) SMB - "Shared folders on your home network or NAS." For example, a shared folder on a Windows PC, a NAS such as Synology or QNAP, or a USB disk plugged into your router. Computer on the internet (S) FTP - "Server folders over FTP and SFTP ." For example, a hosting account over FTP, your own home server over SFTP, or a camera that uploads photos to an FTP folder. In cloud resources - " Google Drive , OneDrive , Dropbox ." For example, sign in to Google Drive once and browse your photo backup like any other folder. Each switch only permits the group - you still add the actual folder or account afterward, from the main screen. The cloud row disappears on an edition without cloud support, and the whole page is left out on an edition with neither group. Turning on network and cloud source groups. Already have a Windows PC on the network? Fast Media Sorter & Sharing for Windows shares chosen PC folders here in a couple of clicks, no server setup needed - this page has a Get the Windows app button for it. 4 Page 4: choose what the app can do "What should the app do?" Turn on what you need - everything here can be changed later in Settings too. The switches: Allow All Files mode (permits it; you still turn it on per resource), Audio , Video , Documents , Text recognition ( OCR ) , Translation , and, on an edition that carries live Streams , a Streams switch that plays internet stations and channels and can import the built-in catalog. Turning on OCR or Translation does more than flip a switch: each one queues a small recognition or translation engine to download right there, with a progress line that counts up and turns into "Ready" when it lands, or "Download failed - tap to retry" if it does not. The capability itself switches on only once its engine has installed successfully, so nothing is left half-enabled. A Statistics collection switch sits lower on the page - on by default, on the Standard, Lite, Photos and Legacy editions - with the note "Collected on your device. Nothing is sent automatically." Below it, on the Standard and noLegal editions, an Enable gestures switch turns on left-edge swipes: up opens the launch menu, right captures a screenshot and opens the editor, down captures one silently with a toast. Every downloadable extra the app offers, not only OCR and translation, is one tap away too: All downloadable (optional) elements opens the extensions manager right over the wizard, so you can browse and install one without losing your place in setup. Turning on capabilities - an OCR engine downloading inline. 5 Page 5: grant the permissions it asks for The permissions page lists every access this particular build can ask for, grouped and explained in plain language, with each row showing whether it is already granted. Grant All walks through every regular permission in one batch dialog, then opens each special one - the kind Android insists on its own settings page for - one at a time; Open App Settings jumps straight to the system screen for anything you would rather set by hand. What the page offers changes with the edition and the Android version on your device, and every permission it can request - including drawing over other apps and installing an app from a file - gets the same explanation wherever the app asks for it again later. The full list, and exactly what each permission unlocks, has its own page: see Storage and system permissions . Granting a permission from the wizard's permissions page. 6 Page 6: make it your default player (first run only) If nothing has claimed the role yet, one more page shows up: Default Player - "Set FastMediaSorter as your default media player." Four buttons, one per type - Audio , Video , Images , Documents - each opens Android's own app chooser. "Tap a button below - a dialog will appear. Select FastMediaSorter and tap Always ." The page explains what that choice actually changes: "Being the default app means a file opened from somewhere else - a gallery, a messenger, a file manager - lands here instead of the system player." And that trying it costs nothing: "This is not permanent: Android keeps the choice in its own settings and it can be changed back at any time." Once you have answered this page, or once FastMediaSorter already is the default for everything it can be, it stops appearing on later runs of the wizard. Setting FastMediaSorter as the default player, one media type at a time. 7 Or skip ahead - the Enable all shortcut On the Standard, Legacy, VR and noLegal editions, a green Enable all button sits on the first page, next to the page dots. Tap it and a dialog explains "What happens next" first: "Android will ask a few questions of its own. You will leave this screen for a moment and come back here automatically." Three short steps follow it - Allow access ("Android shows its own request. Tap Allow. Some kinds of access open a separate settings page instead - turn the switch on there and press Back."), Choose the app for your files ("One of your own files opens so Android can ask which app should handle it. This is expected. Pick FastMediaSorter, tap Always, then press Back to return here."), and Back returns you here ("Every screen that is not ours is left with Back. Nothing is lost - setup continues where it stopped."). Tap Got it, start to continue, or dismiss the dialog and nothing changes. Confirming opens the same device-profile picker from page 2 first, so an unlucky auto-detection is still visible and correctable before anything is applied. From there, Enable all switches on every setting that unlocks a capability your edition ships - image and GIF viewing included, plus every feature route compiled into the build - while leaving privacy, destructive, preference and resource-dependent settings untouched. It also brings back every "Send to.." recipient your edition enables by default - the system share sheet, Open with, Print, Email, Google Keep and the watch - even ones you had switched off earlier, though a recipient the edition ships off by default, such as the messengers or Google Lens, stays off, and one you switched on yourself is never touched. A second reminder appears right before the default-app stage, worded the same way ("One more step: the app for your files.."), with Show me and Skip this buttons. Declining either reminder just leaves that one step unrun - the rest of Enable all still goes ahead. What Enable all is about to do, explained before it starts. 8 Finish, and what happens right after Tap Finish on the last page and the wizard closes. The very first time only, FastMediaSorter opens Settings once on its own, with the main screen waiting behind it - so backing out of Settings lands you on the main screen, not back in the wizard. It never opens Settings uninvited again after that. Changed your mind about the device profile, or want to turn a whole group of sources on or off again? Reopen this same wizard any time from Settings. It warns you first, since running it again can overwrite settings you have since tuned by hand. What You Get The app now speaks your language, looks the way you like, knows what kind of device it is running on, can see the network and cloud folders you turned on, and - if you asked it to - already answers to "Open with" and the system share sheet for the file types it plays. None of this is final: every choice lives in Settings afterward, and the wizard is one tap away if you want to run it again. Tips and Troubleshooting Enable all switches everything on for good. Text recognition and translation stay on even when both of their parts finish installing at the same moment - they no longer switch themselves back off. In a hurry? Enable all on page 1 answers almost every later page for you and finishes setup in a few taps - see step 7 above. Statistics collection stays on the device. The switch on the functionality page only ever writes to local, anonymous numbers; nothing is sent out automatically. Not sure about a permission yet? Skip it here. The permissions guide explains what each one unlocks, and Settings lets you grant it later. Which pages you see depends on the edition. The noLegal edition , for example, shows every page in this recipe; a lighter edition may skip the network page or the default-player page entirely. pages.description: Installing FastMediaSorter, what the first launch splash shows you, a fast honest start on a fresh install, bringing in folders from your Windows PC, and a map of where to read next.
headings: The first thing you see - a splash with a clock
Behind the splash - a fast, honest start
A quick look around, by role
Bring in folders from your Windows PC
pages.body: Getting Started All editions Recipe #04 All editions - install source depends on the edition Quick Product Tour From installing FastMediaSorter to the clock on its first splash to a map of which recipe to read next - this is the five-minute tour before the welcome wizard asks you anything. Why You'll Love This This page is the short version of the whole documentation site: where to get the app, what you see in the seconds after you tap its icon for the first time, and a map of which recipe to open next depending on what you actually want to do with it. If the welcome wizard is the conversation FastMediaSorter has with you once, this page is the five-minute walk around the building before that conversation starts. Nothing here requires a decision. It is a look around, not a checklist. Before You Begin: Ingredients & Prerequisites An Android phone, tablet, TV box, car head unit or headset - FastMediaSorter runs on all of them, in the edition built for that hardware. A way to install an app: the Google Play Store, or a downloaded APK file for the editions that are not sold in a store. For the Windows-folder step: Fast Media Sorter & Sharing for Windows running on the same network as your phone. 1 Get the app The Standard edition is on Google Play, like any other app - search for FastMediaSorter or open its store listing directly and tap Install . The other editions - noLegal, VR, Lite, Photos and Legacy - carry features a store will not list, so they are not sold there. You install one of these by downloading its APK file directly, either from the project's GitHub Releases page or from the IzzyOnDroid repository, and opening it. Android meets a package it has not seen installed from a store before and shows a one-time warning about it; that warning is about how many times Android has seen the file's signature, not about anything found inside it. Why Android warns about this APK, and exactly what to tap walks through both screens. 2 The first thing you see - a splash with a clock Launching the app opens on its own startup splash instead of a bare window: the four-arrow logo arrives in the same blue as the launcher icon, growing into place rather than fading, with the app name and the line "..All mine, here!" beneath it, in the language of your device. Underneath the logo, the current time counts by the second, in your device's own 12- or 24-hour style and time zone - so it reads exactly like your system clock, not like a stopwatch the app started on its own. The splash lasts exactly as long as the app takes to start: if it is ready sooner, the splash is gone sooner, and it disappears together with the clock the moment the app opens. On a first launch that goes straight to the welcome wizard , this splash is skipped - there is nothing yet to jump ahead of. The startup splash, with the clock running underneath it. 3 Behind the splash - a fast, honest start A few things happen while that splash is up, or right after it, that you notice as an absence of problems rather than as a feature: the first thumbnail grid does not stall, because the image loader is built on a background thread instead of on the main thread during your first photo load. The app itself does not stall either, because its file-transfer preferences open on first use instead of while the main screen is still being built. And on a completely fresh install, the built-in collections on the main screen - All Music , All Videos , All Images , Camera Photos and Recent Media - already show their real file counts instead of a row of zeros. FastMediaSorter fills those virtual resource counts in on its own, in the background, at startup, so you do not have to open each one or run a manual rescan just to find out there is anything in it. A fresh install, with real counts already on the built-in collections. 4 A quick look around, by role Page 1 of the welcome wizard pitches FastMediaSorter as a handful of roles rather than a feature list, and this documentation site is organized the same way. Once you have looked around the main screen , here is where each role's own recipes live: File manager - browsing, sorting and file operations start at grid and list views and copy, move and delete . Player - photos and GIFs in the image viewer , video in playback controls , and music in playing and organizing . Any source - local, network and cloud folders start at storage sources setup and Windows network shares . Streams , on the editions that carry it - begins at the channel catalog . More - the desktop launcher , the watch app , the VR headset , and the full Settings map all branch off from here, alongside the seven editions compared . The watch trusts what the phone trusts If you pinned an SFTP server's host key on the phone, the watch app enforces that same pin: a server presenting a different key is refused before your password is ever sent. The pin travels with the source, so there is nothing to set up on the watch itself - see watch companion data sync . 5 Bring in folders from your Windows PC If you run Fast Media Sorter & Sharing for Windows on the same network, you do not have to type in a server address by hand: scan its QR code, or open the .fmscfg file it hands you, and FastMediaSorter adds those PC folders as SFTP resources in one step. Import the same file again later - say, after sharing one more folder on the PC - and it does not create duplicates. It recognizes a resource it already has by its server and folder path and updates that one instead, then shows a short toast telling you what happened: "Added: " or "Updated: " when exactly one resource changed, a combined count when several did, or "Resources already up to date" when nothing did. Re-importing a companion file updates the matching resource instead of duplicating it. What You Get You have the app installed, you know what that first splash is telling you, your built-in collections already show real numbers, and you have a map of which recipe to read next for whatever you actually came here to do - browse files, watch something, or bring in a folder from another machine. Tips and Troubleshooting The splash is honest about timing. It stays up exactly as long as startup actually takes - a faster phone sees it for less time, not a fixed animation length. No servers, no analytics. FastMediaSorter has no backend of its own; nothing about how you use the app is sent anywhere without your say-so. See the privacy policy for the specifics. Re-importing a companion file is always safe. It only adds or updates the resources that changed - it never leaves you with two copies of the same PC folder. Skipped the wizard by accident? It is one tap away from Settings any time - see first launch and setup wizard . What to Try Next: Related Recipes Getting Started First launch and setup wizard Language, theme, device profile, sources, permissions and your default player, page by page. pages.title: Understanding App Permissions
pages.description: What each permission FastMediaSorter can ask for actually unlocks, how to grant one permission at a time or all of them at once, and how to change your mind later in Android
headings: Grant one permission at a time
pages.body: Getting Started All editions Recipe #02 Understanding App Permissions FastMediaSorter only asks for the permissions a feature actually needs, explains each one in the same plain words everywhere it is asked, and lets you grant them one at a time or all at once from Settings, General, Permissions & Access - with Android's own app settings always one tap away for changing your mind later. Why You'll Love This FastMediaSorter only sees and touches what Android lets it. Every permission it can ask for exists because some feature needs it - reading your photos, opening a shared folder over the network, writing a geotag into a picture you just took. Nothing is requested "just in case". You already met a short version of this list on the welcome screen when you first opened the app. This page is the full picture: every permission this edition can ask for, in plain words, in one place, with a way to grant them one at a time or all together. Before You Begin: Ingredients & Prerequisites FastMediaSorter installed, in any edition : Standard, noLegal, Lite, Photos, Legacy, VR or FOSS. The exact list of rows differs a little by edition - a permission only appears if this build can actually use it. A few rows only appear from certain Android versions onward - each one names the version it needs, so there is nothing to look up. 1 Find the full list Open Settings , the General tab, and tap Permissions & Access . The screen lists every permission this edition can request, grouped under headings: Storage , Network , Microphone , Notifications , Camera , Location , System , and - on editions that ship the launcher - Contacts . Each row shows a short label, a one-line description, and whether it is currently granted. The same list, with the same wording, is also the last page of the first-launch setup wizard - see First launch and setup wizard . Settings, General, Permissions & Access. 2 Grant one permission at a time Tap any row that is not yet granted. Most rows show Android's own request dialog right there - tap Allow and you are back on the list. A few permissions cannot be granted this way at all: Android insists on a dedicated screen for them, for example Full storage management or Display over other apps . For those, tapping the row opens that screen; make your choice there and press Back to return to FastMediaSorter. The system's own request dialog for one permission. 3 Grant everything in one go Tap Grant All at the top of the screen instead of working through the rows one by one. The app answers one ordinary Android dialog for the permissions that support it, then walks you to each special-screen permission in turn, one system screen at a time, so you always know which one you are looking at. Changed your mind about a specific one afterwards? Deny it the normal way in Android, or come back to this screen and revisit that single row. Grant All walks through every permission for you. 4 What each group actually unlocks Storage - reading your photos, video and music, and, on the sideload noLegal edition only, full access to any folder for bulk media edits. Network - reaching SMB, SFTP, FTP and DLNA servers on your local network. On newer Android versions this is its own permission, separate from Wi-Fi being on. Microphone - recording voice notes and capturing sound inside screen recordings, on editions that record audio. Notifications - showing progress while a long job runs in the background, on editions that keep audio playing after you leave the app. Camera - taking photos and video inside the app, reading text and scanning QR codes, including the code used to pair a companion device. Location - writing coordinates into the photos and videos you shoot in the app. On editions with a launcher desktop or a Network Monitor, the same permission also drives the compass, speed, altitude and map desktop gadgets and the network monitor's GNSS and Wi-Fi details - the row on those editions names all of that, not only the geotag. System - background items such as an exemption from battery optimization for scheduled jobs, drawing the gesture strip over other apps, installing an APK you opened from a file (noLegal edition only), and reporting phone signal strength or step count on the launcher desktop. Contacts - reading a pinned contact's current name and photo so a launcher shortcut stays up to date, on editions with a launcher desktop. A row you do not see simply does not apply to this edition or this Android version - the list never hides a permission the app could still use. Image Bookmark [Planned] Screenshot: Permission groups Settings, Permissions, scrolled down past Camera. Profile: phone ID: getting-started.permissions-groups One wording, everywhere Whichever screen asks for a permission - this list, the welcome wizard, or a dialog shown while you work - it explains that permission in the same words. Nothing changes meaning depending on where you happened to be asked. 5 Change a decision later Tap Open App Settings to jump straight to Android's own application details screen for FastMediaSorter. That is the only place to grant a permission Android has stopped asking about in-app - typically one you denied twice in a row - and it is also where you go to revoke something you granted earlier. Android's own app settings screen. What You Get You know what every permission this edition can ask for is actually for, you can grant them one at a time or all in one pass, and you know exactly where to go in Android when you want to revisit a choice later. Tips and Troubleshooting Audio permissions are always offered where they belong. In the editions that record or play sound in the background, the microphone and audio permissions are listed and can be granted - they are never hidden by mistake. A row named 'Physical activity' or 'Install apps from files'? Those only appear on the noLegal sideload edition, because only its manifest declares them - the Play Store edition never shows a permission it could not act on. Location reads differently depending on your edition. On Standard and noLegal it explains the desktop gadgets and Network Monitor too; on the others it stays a plain geotag explanation, because that is all those editions use it for. A denied permission is not a dead end. Most features that need one keep working in a reduced form, and a row you skip during setup stays visible here for whenever you change your mind. What to Try Next: Related Recipes Getting Started First launch and setup wizard The short version of this same permissions list, on the last page of first setup. pages.title: Navigating the Main Screen
pages.description: What the resource list, the command bar, the resource-type tabs and the programs and streams panels do, how to sort and filter your resources, and how to read the recording indicator and the reconnect prompt.
headings: The command bar across the top
Filter by type with the tabs
Sort and filter the resource list
More on one resource - the three-dots menu
pages.body: Getting Started All editions Recipe #03 Navigating the Main Screen The main screen is your home base: a resource list with All Files pinned first, a command bar that never runs out of room, tabs and optional panels that fit any screen width, and a filter and sort dialog that remembers your choice - with a corner pill to tell you when something is recording. Why You'll Love This The main screen is where every session with FastMediaSorter starts and usually ends. It is the one screen that has to make sense at a glance whether you have three resources or thirty - a folder on the phone, a shared drive at home, a handful of streams - so knowing what each part of it does saves you a few taps every single time you open the app. Nothing here changes your files. This page is a map of the screen, not a set of actions to perform. Before You Begin: Ingredients & Prerequisites FastMediaSorter in any edition : Standard, noLegal, Lite, Photos, Legacy, VR or FOSS. A couple of pieces described here - the streams panel and the paired-watch filter - only exist on editions that ship streams or a Wear OS companion. At least one resource added, so the list and the panels have something to show. See Setting up local and removable storage if you have not added one yet. 1 Read the resource list Your resources - folders, network shares, cloud accounts, streams and anything else you have added - are shown as rows or tiles in the resource list . The All Files resource, where it exists on this edition, always stays first no matter how you sort the rest, unless a tab or a filter hides it entirely. Long-press and drag any other resource to put it where you want it; the app remembers the new order. Tap View on the command bar to switch the whole list between rows (list view) and tiles (grid view). The resource list, in grid view. 2 The command bar across the top The row of buttons above the list - Exit , Add , Filter , Refresh , Settings , View , Favorites and Start Player - is always there, though not always with its text labels. On a narrow screen the labels disappear first so every icon still fits; if icons alone still do not fit, the buttons at the right give way one at a time into the More actions (three-dots) menu, so a command is never simply cut off the edge of the screen. Buttons that do not fit move into More actions. Everything still reachable A command that moved into the three-dots menu works exactly the same as it did on the bar - it just needs one extra tap to find. Nothing you can do on a wide screen becomes unavailable on a narrow one. 3 Filter by type with the tabs Just under the command bar sits a row of resource-type tabs - ALL and Local , plus SMB , S/FTP and Cloud on editions that have them - that narrow the resource list to one kind of resource with a single tap. Each tab takes a share of the available width rather than a fixed size, so every tab stays visible and tappable, Cloud included, in portrait, landscape and on the widest layouts. Every resource-type tab fits, even on a narrow screen. 4 The programs and streams panels Two optional bars can sit above the resource list: the programs panel for one-tap access to the app's built-in programs (see Built-in programs ), and, on editions that ship streams, the streams panel for your pinned channels (see Browsing internet stream channels ). Turn either on or off in Settings. On a wide layout the two panels and the tab strip line up on one shared grid, using the programs panel's own button width as the common measure. If the screen is too narrow for a panel to show in full, its icon collapses into a small chip that moves into the free space at the end of the command bar row instead of taking a row of its own - unless the command bar is already full, in which case the chip keeps its own row. The programs panel and the streams panel, above the resource list. 5 Sort and filter the resource list Tap Filter to open the Filter and Sort Resources dialog. From there you can filter by resource type, filter by the media types a resource supports, and choose a sort order. On Standard and noLegal you can also filter by a paired watch's own resource type. Whatever you choose here is remembered and reapplied the next time you open the app - even after the app is force-stopped or the phone restarts - and a banner above the list reminds you which filters are currently on, so a short list reads as filtered rather than as resources gone missing. Full details: Sorting, filtering and quick search . The Filter and Sort Resources dialog. Cell size for grid view Prefer bigger or smaller tiles? Go to Settings, General, and set Resource grid cell size to Small, Medium or Large - it scales whatever column count your screen and orientation already use. 6 More on one resource - the three-dots menu Open the three-dots menu on any resource row for the actions that do not fit as icons - renaming, removing, and Reconnect resource for a folder that needs its connection refreshed. If the folder you pick during a reconnect does not match what the resource pointed to before, a confirmation dialog asks you to double-check before it is applied - and that dialog now stays on screen if you rotate the phone while it is open, instead of quietly disappearing. Actions for one resource live in its three-dots menu. 7 The recording indicator While a screen recording or a quick voice capture is running, a small pill appears in a corner of the screen - a dot, a timer, and pause/resume and stop buttons - so you can check on or stop the recording without leaving the main screen. It now shows up reliably on wide landscape layouts too, such as a car head unit, where it used to stay invisible. See Recording the device screen with audio . The recording indicator, while a recording is running. What You Get You can read the resource list at a glance, reach every command whether or not the screen has room for its label, narrow the list with the tabs and the filter dialog, tell at a glance when something is recording, and know where to look when a resource needs reconnecting. Tips and Troubleshooting Built-in resources speak your language. Recent Media, All Music, All Files, Downloads and the other ready-made resources rename themselves the moment you switch the app's language, instead of staying in whatever language was active on first launch. A fresh install still shows real numbers. The file count on the built-in collections fills in shortly after install, in the background, instead of sitting at zero until you open each one. The Programs button stays centered. Its icon and label sit in the middle of their cell in both the regular and the compact command bar, so it lines up with its neighbors either way. What to Try Next: Related Recipes Getting Started Understanding app permissions What each permission unlocks, before you start adding resources. pages.description: What the startup splash shows, which notifications the app posts and how to silence each kind, the one color each type of content and each program keeps everywhere, hiding password screens from the recent-apps list, and the app
headings: Read the notifications - and silence the ones you do not need
Hide password screens from the recent-apps list
Choosing the app language and units
pages.body: General, Keyboard & TV All editions Recipe #04 All editions - each notification appears only in the editions that have its feature Notifications, the Startup Splash and Colors - How the App Shows Itself The startup splash, the notifications, the colors of content types and programs, private password screens and one language everywhere - the ways FastMediaSorter shows itself around the phone. Why You'll Love This An app does not live only on its own screens. It greets you when it starts, it tells you about a long copy in the notification shade, and it colors a photo differently from a song so you can tell them apart at a glance. This page walks through all of these small meeting points, so you know what each one means and how to change it when you want it quieter. Before You Begin: Ingredients & Prerequisites FastMediaSorter in any edition . 1 Meet the startup splash For the moment the app takes to start, the startup splash shows the FastMediaSorter logo and the name Fast Media Sorter fading in at the center, with a small author logo at the bottom center and a clock ticking below the logo - in the 24-hour or 12-hour style you chose for units. It disappears by itself as soon as the app is ready; tapping it does nothing, so a stray tap does not press anything behind it. Image Bookmark [Planned] Screenshot: Startup splash Phone, cold start of the app, the startup splash with the logo, the name, the ticking clock and the author logo. Profile: phone ID: general.startup-splash 2 Read the notifications - and silence the ones you do not need Every FastMediaSorter notification carries the app logo in the status bar, so you always know where it came from - a file copy or a duplicate search no longer shows the music note of the audio player . Android groups the notifications into categories, and you can switch each category off separately. The categories are: Audio Playback - what is playing, with play, pause and skip buttons. Scheduled operations - progress of a scheduled operation . Network Sync Settings - background sync of a network resource . Duplicate scanner - progress of a duplicate search. Link downloads - files downloaded from a shared or pasted link; these pop up at the top of the screen. Browse file transfers - a copy or a move running in the background. Element Downloads - downloadable parts of the app, such as an extension . Files from the watch - a file received from the paired watch being saved. Voice recording - the quick voice recorder at work. Save fallback - a file could not be saved in the usual place and was saved elsewhere. Flashlight shortcut - a notification that turns the flashlight on and off. SOS signal - the SOS program is running. SFTP server - the app's own SFTP server is running. To switch a category off, long-press any FastMediaSorter notification and tap the settings icon, or open the phone's Settings , Apps , FastMediaSorter , Notifications . Google's notification help shows the same on your phone model. Image Bookmark [Planned] Screenshot: Notification categories Android Settings, Apps, FastMediaSorter, Notifications, the list of categories with switches. Profile: phone ID: general.notification-categories Keep the progress ones If you switch off the file transfer or scheduled operation categories, the work still runs - you just do not see its progress. Keep them on if you like to know when a big copy is done. 3 Recognize content by its color Each type of content has one color, and it is the same everywhere: in the statistics chart, on the small badges of each row of the resource list and on the resource icons. Before, a screen could pick its own shade, so one type looked three different ways; now one color always means one type, and every color has a matching shade for the dark theme. The same goes for programs : each has its own color and keeps it in the programs menu, the programs panel and its overflow, the quick-launch grid, the launcher desktop, the widget picker and the pinned widget on the home screen. Image Bookmark [Planned] Screenshot: Content type colors Main screen, resource list with several resources, each row showing its colored media-type badges. Profile: phone ID: general.content-type-colors 4 Hide password screens from the recent-apps list Screens where a password may be visible - adding or editing a network or server resource , the stored-credentials editor in Settings , the sign-in page in the browser and the credentials barcode - show up blank in the recent-apps list and cannot be captured in a screenshot . The switch is Secure sensitive screens in Settings , General , Authorization and accounts , and it is on from the start. All other screens stay free to capture. More privacy settings: Privacy, passcodes and network security . 5 One language on every screen The app speaks thirteen languages, and the one you choose is used on every screen - also on the few that used to follow the phone's language instead: the watch companion window, the screens that open from a widget , the barcode import from the Windows companion , the permission screens for camera and screen capture, the launcher's own screens and both VR screens. After a change, every cell and section title of the launcher desktop switches too, and the choice sticks - it does not slip back to the old language. Text that is not translated yet appears in English. In the same settings group, the Unit system row shows its value right next to its name, like every other row. How to pick the language and the units: Choosing the app language and units . What You Get You know what the startup splash, the notifications and the colors are telling you, how to quiet any notification category, and how password screens stay private. Tips and Troubleshooting Too many notifications? Switch off just the categories you do not need - the work behind them keeps running. Using the app on a TV? See Keyboard, D-pad and TV control . Backing up everything before a new phone? See Backing up and restoring settings .
