pages.title: Product Overview & Architecture Guide
pages.description: Comprehensive overview of Fast Media Sorter: core features, multi-platform architecture (Phones, TV, Wear OS, VR), 7 editions, and guide to the full documentation cookbook.
pages.body: Official Guide Multi-Platform 105 Recipes Fast Media Sorter - Product Overview Fast Media Sorter is a high-performance, privacy-first multimedia organizer, universal media player, and desktop environment designed for Android phones, tablets, TVs, Wear OS smartwatches, and OpenXR VR headsets. Fast Media Sorter is built on eight pillars, in this order: device shell, media player, live streams, app launching, a replacement for stock apps, a companion on the watch, device monitoring and a full file manager. Browse All 22 Categories A-Z Subject Index PDF Offline Handbook What is Fast Media Sorter? Traditional mobile gallery and file manager apps are built for casual viewing. When dealing with thousands of photos, gigabytes of lossless music, sprawling video libraries, network storage (NAS), and cloud drives, standard tools become sluggish and cumbersome. Fast Media Sorter is engineered from the ground up to solve this: Lightning Fast One-Tap Sorting Sort, move, and copy files to predefined targets with a single tap, gesture, or keyboard shortcut. Universal Playback Any Format & Source Seamless playback for FLAC, MKV, MP4, PDF, EPUB, M3U streams, and cloud/network storage without local copying. Zero Telemetry 100% Privacy & Offline No analytics trackers, no account required, all sorting and statistics remain strictly on your local device. Ecosystem Watch & VR Companion Sync playlists, control playback from your wrist, or view 3D/180° spatial cinema in OpenXR VR headsets. Supported Platforms & Form Factors Fast Media Sorter adapts its UI and input handling to each specific form factor: Platform Optimizations & Key Features Guides Android Smartphones & Tablets Touch gestures, multi-window split-screen, foldables, edge quick-access panel, PIP video, photo editor, OCR & translation. Setup , Browsing Android TV & Media Boxes Complete D-Pad / remote control support, high contrast large-screen UI, live stream catalog, Chromecast casting receiver/sender. TV & D-Pad Guide Wear OS Smartwatches Standalone music & streams playback, watch file manager, tiles, complications, flashlight, SOS, health & step metrics. Watch Suite Meta Quest & OpenXR VR Curved spatial cinema, 3D SBS/OU, 180° and 360° hemispherical video, room passthrough, controller and hand tracking. VR Guide The Seven Editions (Flavors) To comply with different distribution channels (Google Play, F-Droid, Meta Horizon Store, legacy Android devices) while providing maximal capabilities, Fast Media Sorter is published in 7 distinct editions: Standard Standard Edition The flagship build for Google Play. Full feature set including media player, sorting, cloud integration, OCR, desktop launcher, and Wear companion. FOSS F-Droid / FOSS Edition 100% libre software with zero proprietary binary dependencies (no Google Drive / Play Services). Fully reproducible builds. Lite Lite Edition Ultra-compact footprint for resource-constrained devices, focusing strictly on core file management, browsing, and sorting. Photos Photos Edition Specialized for digital photo frames and photography enthusiasts. Features advanced slideshows, EXIF tools, and gallery curation. Legacy Legacy Edition Backwards-compatible edition optimized for older Android versions (API 21+) and vintage media tablets. VR VR Edition Standalone OpenXR package built for Meta Quest headsets with spatial immersive cinema and hands-free controls. NoLegal Direct / NoLegal Edition Direct APK distribution with unrestricted local and network stream codecs, SFTP/SMB servers, and power-user utilities. Detailed edition matrix and side-by-side feature comparison: Read Editions, Extensions & Languages Guide → Core Subsystems & 22 Thematic Cookbook Chapters The documentation corpus consists of 105 in-depth recipes across 22 thematic areas. Here is how the system is structured: Orientation 1. Getting Started & Editions Setup wizard, permission management, editions comparison, and localization settings. Explore Getting Started → Organization 2. Browsing & Storage Grid/list views, thumbnail indexing, batch operations, destination setup, and secure PIN containers. Explore Browsing & Storage → Networking 3. Network & Cloud Storage SMB/Samba, SFTP/FTP, Google Drive, OneDrive, Dropbox, and the Windows Companion app. Explore Network & Cloud → Playback 4. Video, Audio & Photo Player Lossless FLAC playback, audio queues, MKV video controls, subtitles, PIP, and photo editors. Explore Players → Reading & Streaming 5. Documents & Internet Streams PDF/EPUB viewers, Markdown text editor, live M3U radio and TV channel catalogs, and buffering tools. Explore Documents & Streams → Capture & OCR 6. Camera, Recording & OCR Tools Quick snaps, screen recording, annotation markups, optical text recognition (OCR), and translation. Explore Capture & Tools → Desktop & Tools 7. Launcher, Gadgets & Mini-Apps Full home-screen replacement desktop, taskbar dock, weather/clock gadgets, calculator, and SOS lights. Explore Launcher → Configuration 8. Settings & Diagnostics Preferences search, key remapping for gamepads/remotes, system diagnostics, and configuration backup. Explore Settings → Wear OS & VR 9. Wear OS Smartwatch & VR Headsets Wear standalone player, tiles, sync companion, and OpenXR 3D spatial cinema playback. Explore Watch & VR → Quick Start Guide in 3 Steps Step 1: Welcome Setup Wizard On initial launch, Fast Media Sorter detects your device hardware (smartphone, TV box, tablet, or car unit) and recommends an optimized preset. Choose your preferred language, theme, and grant storage permissions. Step-by-step Setup Walkthrough → Step 2: Add Sources & Destination Targets Select which local folders, SD cards, SMB network shares, or cloud storage accounts to monitor. Configure your Quick Sort destination buttons (e.g. Favorites , Work , Archive , To Review ). Configuring Sources & Destinations → Step 3: Browse, Play & One-Tap Sort Swipe through media with full gesture controls. When organizing, tap a destination icon or press a remapped key to instantly move or copy the current item and advance to the next file. File Operations & Sorting Guide → Where to Go Next Explore the full documentation using any of the available discovery mechanisms: Table of Contents Complete Table of Contents Browse all 22 thematic categories containing links to every single cookbook recipe. pages.title: Playing and Organizing Music Files
pages.description: How to play music from any folder, get album covers and lyrics from the internet, choose an animated background for tracks without a cover, send music to a Chromecast, and sort tracks into folders while you listen.
headings: Get missing album covers from the internet
Pick a background for tracks without a cover
Read the lyrics or find the song on YouTube Music
Playback order, sleep timer and listening in the background
pages.body: Images, Audio & Slideshow Standard, noLegal, Lite, Legacy, VR and FOSS Recipe #04 Playing and Organizing Music Files Play music straight from the folders where it lives - on the phone, a memory card or another computer. The audio player finds missing covers, shows lyrics, casts to a Chromecast and lets you sort tracks while you listen. Why You'll Love This Your music does not live in one neat library. Some albums are on the phone, some on a memory card, some on the computer in the next room. FastMediaSorter plays music straight from the folders where it already is - no importing, no library to build - and lets you sort a messy download folder while you listen. The same audio player finds missing album covers, shows song lyrics, and fills the screen with a calm animation when a track has no picture. Before You Begin: Ingredients & Prerequisites FastMediaSorter in the Standard, noLegal, Lite, Legacy, VR or FOSS edition . The Photos edition does not play audio. Music files in any common format: MP3, FLAC, AAC, M4A, OGG, Opus, WMA, WAV, ALAC and more. MIDI files (MID, MIDI) play too. A resource that holds your music - for example the ready-made All Music collection, a folder on this device, or a network folder . For covers and lyrics from the internet: an internet connection. For Chromecast: a Chromecast on the same Wi-Fi network, and any edition except VR and FOSS. 1 Open a track Open a resource with music on the main screen and tap a track in the file browser . The audio player opens and starts playing. The screen shows the album cover, the track name and details such as size, format and sample rate, a progress bar you can drag, and the playback buttons. A small spinning vinyl record in the corner tells you at a glance that music is playing; it stops when you pause. When the track ends, the player moves on to the next audio file of the same folder. Swipe left or right, or use the next and previous buttons, to skip. The audio player with an album cover and the spinning vinyl record in the corner. 2 Get missing album covers from the internet Most music files carry their own cover picture, and the player shows it right away. For files without one, the app can look the cover up online. Go to Settings , the Media tab, section Audio playback, covers and visuals , and turn on Search audio covers online . It is off until you turn it on. The app then asks three free music catalogs in turn - iTunes, Deezer and the Cover Art Archive - and shows the first good cover it finds. Two more switches appear below: Search only on Wi-Fi (on by default, so no mobile data is used) and Save downloaded media data locally (on by default, so each cover is fetched only once). Online cover search in Settings. 3 Pick a background for tracks without a cover When no cover can be found, the screen does not have to stay empty. In the same settings section tap Visualizer when no cover art and choose one: Black background - nothing moves. Music note + pulse rings - a music note with rings pulsing around it. Breathing bars (15) - soft colored bars rising and falling like an equalizer. Wave & Particle Animation - flowing waves with drifting particles. Visualization (MP4) - one of several looping video clips. The clips are not part of the app; the first time you choose this, the app offers to download them. Instead of an animation you can also show your own photos: turn on Show random photos during audio playback , tap Select Photos Source and choose a resource with pictures. A different photo from it appears for each song. See Creating photo slideshows to let the photos change during a song. Wave & Particle Animation behind a track without a cover. 4 Read the lyrics or find the song on YouTube Music Open the three-dots menu and tap Lyrics . The app searches the internet for the words of the song, using the artist and title stored in the file or its file name, and shows them full screen. Tap the close button to return to the player. The text size follows the Text Settings you use for translations. To hear another version of the song or explore the artist, tap In YouMusic on the command panel or in the three-dots menu. The YouTube Music app opens with a search for the current track. If YouTube Music is not installed, a short message tells you so. Lyrics shown full screen. 5 Play on a Chromecast Tap the cast button Cast to.. on the command panel and pick your Chromecast or smart TV from the list. The music plays on it, and the phone becomes the remote control. The same button sends photos, GIFs and videos too; see casting and broadcast . Files from a network folder or cloud storage are first copied to the phone and then sent to the Chromecast, so the first seconds may take a moment. The phone and the Chromecast must be on the same Wi-Fi network. Image Bookmark [Planned] Screenshot: Cast device list Cast route chooser dialog over the audio player, one device listed. Profile: phone ID: audio.cast-device-picker 6 Sort tracks while you listen A download folder full of unsorted songs is easiest to clean up by ear. While a track plays, tap Copy to.. or Move to.. at the bottom of the player and pick a destination folder - for example "Keep", "Car" or "Delete later". The player continues with the next track, so you can sort a whole folder in one listening session. How destinations are set up is explained in Copy, move and delete files . What You Get Your music plays from wherever it is stored, with covers found automatically, lyrics one tap away, a calm animation or your own photos when there is no cover, and a Chromecast when you want the big speakers. A messy folder gets sorted while you listen. Tips and Troubleshooting A WAV file opened a menu instead of playing? Current versions open WAV files in the audio player directly. Update the app if you still see the menu. Covers do not appear? Check that Search audio covers online is on, and that you are on Wi-Fi if Search only on Wi-Fi is on. Very rare recordings may simply not be in the catalogs. Cast button missing? The VR and FOSS editions do not include Chromecast support. Also check that Wi-Fi is on. Want the music to keep playing after you leave the player? See Playback order, sleep timer and listening in the background . pages.title: Playback Order, Sleep Timer and Listening in the Background
pages.description: How to shuffle or repeat the tracks of a folder, fall asleep to music with the sleep timer, keep listening while you use other apps, and control playback from the notification, the Quick Settings tile and the watch.
headings: Fall asleep to music with the sleep timer
Keep listening while you use other apps
Picture-in-picture and background play for video
pages.body: Images, Audio & Slideshow Standard, noLegal, Lite, Legacy, VR and FOSS Recipe #05 All editions except Photos; background listening not in Lite Playback Order, Sleep Timer and Listening in the Background Decide in which order the tracks of a folder play, let the sleep timer stop the music gently, and keep listening while you use other apps - with controls in the notification, a Quick Settings tile and the Now Playing bar. Why You'll Love This Music rarely has your full attention. You listen while you cook, walk, read the news or fall asleep. This recipe covers everything that happens around the tracks: in which order they play, how to stop the music by itself after half an hour, and how to keep it going while you do something else. There is no separate playlist to build. The queue is simply the audio files of the folder you opened, in the order the folder is sorted. To change what plays, open a different folder or sort this one differently. Before You Begin: Ingredients & Prerequisites FastMediaSorter in the Standard, noLegal, Lite, Legacy, VR or FOSS edition . The Photos edition does not play audio. Listening in the background, the notification controls and the Quick Settings tile: Standard, noLegal, Legacy, VR and FOSS. In the Lite edition the music stops when you leave the player. A folder with a few tracks, opened in the audio player as described in Playing and organizing music files . 1 Choose the playback order Tap the repeat button at the left of the playback buttons. Each tap switches to the next mode, and a short message confirms it, for example "Playback order: Shuffle": Loop list - plays the folder from top to bottom, then starts again. Play through - plays the folder once and stops at the end. Shuffle - plays the tracks of the folder in random order. Repeat one - plays the current track again and again. After Repeat one the next tap brings you back to Loop list . One button cycles through the four playback orders. 2 Fall asleep to music with the sleep timer Open the three-dots menu and tap Sleep Timer . Choose 15, 30, 45, 60, 90 or 120 minutes. A small badge in the player shows how much time is left, for example "25m" or "1h 10m". When the time runs out, the music does not stop abruptly: it fades out gently over ten seconds and then pauses. To cancel a running timer, open Sleep Timer again and choose Off . Choose when the music should stop. 3 Keep listening while you use other apps Leave the player with the Back button while a track plays. The first time, the app asks "Music is playing in the background. What would you like to do?" - tap Keep Playing to go on listening, or Stop . The same window offers Always Continue and Always Stop if you do not want to be asked again. You can change that choice later in Settings , the Player tab: When leaving player or streams offers Ask every time (default) , Always stop and Always keep playing . The app asks what to do with the music when you leave the player. 4 Control the music from anywhere While music plays in the background you have several remote controls: The Now Playing bar - a small bar at the bottom of the other screens of the app, for example while you look at photos. It shows the track name and its cover; a slowly turning music note replaces the cover when there is none, and it stops turning when you pause. Tap the bar to open Now Playing with the full controls. The bar can be switched off with Show now-playing panel in Settings , the Player tab. The notification - pull down the Android notification shade to see the track and the play, pause and skip buttons. The same controls appear on the lock screen and work with Bluetooth headphones. The Quick Settings tile - add the FMS Audio tile to your Quick Settings panel (pull the shade down twice, tap the pencil and drag the tile in). One tap pauses or resumes; when nothing is playing it starts your music. The Now Playing bar while you browse other files. 5 Calls and other apps When a call comes in or another app starts playing sound, FastMediaSorter pauses the music at once. It does not start again by itself when the call ends - press play when you are ready. If another music app takes over for good, the player stops. 6 On a Wear OS watch The watch app has its own audio player. The current volume is always shown as a bar along the left edge of the screen; it brightens while you turn the bezel to change the volume and dims afterwards. In the Actions menu, the playback mode entry switches between Sequential playback , Shuffle playback and Loop playback with each tap, without closing the menu. More in music on the watch . Image Bookmark [Planned] Screenshot: Watch audio player Wear round screen, audio player playing, volume bar bright after a bezel turn. Profile: wear-round ID: audio.wear-player-volume What You Get Your tracks play in the order you like, the music fades out by itself when you fall asleep, and you can leave the player, answer a call or use other apps while keeping the music under control from the notification, the Now Playing bar, the Quick Settings tile or your watch. Tips and Troubleshooting Want a specific set of songs? Put them in one folder (or copy them there with Copy to.. ) and open that folder. Sort it by name to choose the order. Music stops when you leave the player? Check When leaving player or streams in Settings, Player. In the Lite edition background listening is not available. Music did not resume after a call? That is intentional - press play. It avoids music starting loudly at a bad moment. Playlists of online radio stations are a different thing - see custom M3U playlists . pages.title: Multi-Selection and Batch Operations
pages.description: How to select several files at once with long-press and range-select, run copy, move, delete, share or archive on the whole batch in one tap, act on a single file from its own menu or a swipe, and keep a large copy or move running in the background.
headings: Run one action on the whole selection
Act on one file with the three-dots menu
Swipe a row for an instant action
Let a big copy or move run in the background
pages.body: Browsing & Sorting All editions Recipe #03 Multi-Selection and Batch Operations Tick as many files as you need with long-press and range-select, then run Copy, Move, Delete, Share or Archive on the whole batch at once from the file browser - or reach for a single file's own three-dots menu or a row swipe when that is all the job calls for. Why You'll Love This Some jobs need more than one file at a time - clearing out a folder of screenshots, moving a week of photos to a backup drive, sharing five files with a friend in one go. FastMediaSorter lets you tick as many files as you need and run one action on all of them at once, while a swipe or the row's own menu still covers the times you only want to act on a single file. A copy or move of many files can take a while, especially over a network. It keeps running in the background once you send it there, so you are never stuck staring at a progress bar. Before You Begin: Ingredients & Prerequisites FastMediaSorter installed, with a resource open in the file browser . Multi-selection, the grouped file menu, row swipe actions and the background transfer strip are part of every edition : Standard, noLegal, Lite, Photos, Legacy, VR and FOSS. Write access to the resource for Move, Rename, Delete and Archive - a read-only resource still allows Copy and Share. 1 Select more than one file Long-press any file to enter selection mode. A checkbox appears on every row, and the file you pressed is already ticked. Long-press the checkbox of another file and every file between the two gets selected in one go, instead of ticking each one by hand. Select All and Deselect All in the top bar cover the two extremes, and tapping a checked box again removes just that one file from the selection. Long-press a checkbox to select every file in between. 2 Run one action on the whole selection Once you have files selected, a bar of actions appears at the bottom: Copy , Move , Delete , Share and, on this device's own storage, Archive . Tap one and it runs on every selected file at once. If you deleted or moved something by mistake, Undo appears in the same bar right after, for as long as FastMediaSorter still remembers the operation. Rename shows up on the bar too, but it only opens a dialog when exactly one file is selected - renaming a batch of files at once is a separate tool. Copying and moving need a destination resource to send files to; see Moving, copying and deleting files . The batch action bar appears once you select files. 3 Act on one file with the three-dots menu Tap the three-dots menu on any row to open its own menu instead. The most common actions - Open, Copy, Move, Rename and Delete - sit right at the top, one tap away. Everything else is grouped so the menu never turns into a long scroll: Organize (Favorite, Move up and Move down in the grid, Extract for a ZIP archive, Open in new window, and FileDO encryption), Text (search, translate and OCR for documents, books and images), Editing (crop, draw over, save a frame) and Share and info (send elsewhere, file information, print, lyrics). Only the groups that make sense for that file's type show up. A group with a single action is not a submenu at all: that action sits at the top level, which is why Favorite often appears right under Delete. The per-file menu, grouped into submenus. 4 Swipe a row for an instant action In the file list, a swipe left or right runs one action without opening any menu. Out of the box, one direction deletes and the other opens Send to.. , but you can pick a different action for either direction - or turn a direction off - in Settings, the General tab, File browser interface section, under Swipe left action and Swipe right action . While the row slides, it names the action it is about to run, so a swipe you did not mean to start can be let go before it fires. Deleting by swipe asks for the same confirmation as deleting from a menu, and an action turned off in Settings stays unavailable to the gesture too. Swiping a row reveals the action before it runs. Reaches every edition Row swipe actions work in every edition. 5 Let a big copy or move run in the background Starting a copy or move on a batch opens a progress dialog. Tap Background and the operation keeps running while you carry on browsing. A slim strip then sits at the bottom of Browse, naming the operation, the percent done and the file currently being copied - tap the strip any time to bring the progress dialog back. A backgrounded copy stays visible on a tappable strip. What You Get You can gather up a whole batch with long-press and range-select and send it off with one tap, reach for a single file's own menu or a swipe when that is all you need, and keep a big transfer going in the background without losing sight of it. Tips and Troubleshooting Changed your mind about a swipe? Slide the row back before letting go, or turn that direction off in Settings if you never use it. Renaming several files at once? That needs its own tool - see Batch Renaming Patterns . Selecting with a keyboard or D-pad? Extend the selection up or down without touching the screen - see Keyboard, D-pad and TV navigation . Only seeing Copy and Share on the bar? Move, Rename, Delete and Archive need write access to the resource - a read-only resource hides them on purpose.
